title: Stop the convoy: blockade at the gate
event: Warhead components move by road from the Burghfield assembly plant to Coulport four or five times a year, in a convoy of twenty-odd vehicles that travels at night on public motorways through nine counties. The Ministry publishes no schedule and the local authorities along the route are notified but not consulted. A blockade at the Burghfield gate has been called for the morning of the next movement window.
where: The main gate, Royal Ordnance Factory Burghfield, Reading, Berkshire
function: A protest call: get bodies to a gate at five in the morning, forty miles from anywhere most of them live. Handed out at meetings, pinned in bookshops and posted to a mailing list.
stakes: Turning up means arrest, and the poster is asking for that in advance from people who will read it alone. It has to be honest about the cost and still worth acting on.

hard_constraints.why: A blockade is a time and a place or it is nothing at all.
The named site is the difference between an action and a sentiment, and it is the fact the Ministry would prefer unpublished.
Five in the morning is the whole ask. Concealing the hour to make the poster more appealing would be lying to the people it is recruiting.

notes: No organisation is to be named on the poster; the call is unattributed by request.
